champion: SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
ordered_diagnoses: SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome with meningioma

facts.raw_span: multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules located on the face and vulva
The lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased to approximately 60 lesions
Medical history was significant for a meningioma
Family history was notable for a daughter with similar facial papules that had not undergone biopsy
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Radiographic studies did not reveal any jaw cysts
A conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene (c.757-2A>G) in all tumor and normal tissue samples
Additional distinct deletions of the trans SUFU allele in all tumor samples
No deletions present in the normal sample

concepts.why: The patient's multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules, family history of similar lesions, and genetic findings of a SUFU gene mutation are consistent with Gorlin syndrome.
The patient's skin lesions, histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells, and clefting between tumor aggregates are characteristic of basal cell carcinoma.
The patient's histopathology showing infundibulocystic features is consistent with infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma.
The patient's medical history of meningioma is a relevant finding that may be associated with Gorlin syndrome.

concepts.preferred_label: SUFU-related multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
concepts.why: The patient's genetic findings of a SUFU gene mutation and multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas are consistent with this rare condition.
The patient's family history of similar lesions and multiple basal cell carcinomas is consistent with a familial condition.

concepts.preferred_label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome with meningioma
concepts.why: The patient's combination of nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome and meningioma is a rare but recognized association.
The patient's family history and genetic findings are consistent with a hereditary form of basal cell carcinoma.
